headline: Brighton stun Man City again as Anfield looms
paragraphs: Manchester City lost 1-0 at home to Brighton on Saturday — their second straight Premier League defeat under Enzo Maresca, decided by Yasin Ayari's 11th-minute strike. This is the best-confirmed story in today's feed: Sky Sports, the Guardian and Opta Analyst each filed independent match reports on the same result, three separate newsrooms rather than one story syndicated around, which is as close to settled fact as this feed offers for any of the six clubs.

Liverpool host Arsenal at Anfield on Sunday, and the preview coverage is heavy but it is preview, not news: the Guardian ran separate pieces on Alexis Mac Allister's revival and on Mikel Arteta chasing a first Anfield win in 13 league games, while Opta's model favors Liverpool — three takes on one fixture, not three confirmations of a fact. Separately, Trent Alexander-Arnold's future is unsettled and contradictory across single-sourced tier-one gossip: one report says Liverpool do not plan to bring him back, another (Transfermarkt) says he has been approached about a return, and a third links him with Chelsea instead.

Bayern Munich played Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker Saturday; Harry Kane presented his Ballon d'Or trophy to the Allianz Arena crowd beforehand, per Sky Sports, and a live-blog snapshot had Michael Olise hitting the post, but no final score appears in this feed, so the result is not settled here. Real Madrid's only item is Jose Mourinho, per BBC Sport, declining to elaborate on Kylian Mbappe's Mao Zedong remark while backing his player — commentary from a single outlet, not transfer news.
